*   $\tilde{x}_n$ and $\tilde{x}_{n+1}$ are the endpoints of the $n$-th segment [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the technique computes global light transport by 'dividing rays into k segments'. The mathematical formula provided in the evidence is $L_i(	ilde{x}, 	ilde{ω}_i) = L_0 · ∏_{n=0}^{k} T(	ilde{x}_n, 	ilde{x}_{n+1})$. In this product notation, the index $n$ iterates from 0 to $k$, representing the segments. The term $T(	ilde{x}_n, 	ilde{x}_{n+1})$ represents the transmittance between points $	ilde{x}_n$ and $	ilde{x}_{n+1}$. Since the product runs over $n$ segments (from $n=0$ to $n=k-1$ effectively, or indices $0$ to $k$ defining the boundaries), the points $	ilde{x}_n$ and $	ilde{x}_{n+1}$ serve as the start and end points (endpoints) of the $n$-th segment in the sequence of divided ray segments.
